name: Massachusetts
agency: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau

rule.hpNote: any motorboat (any vessel with machinery propulsion, PWC included)
rule.phaseIn: Hanson-Milone Act: born after Jan. 1, 1989 from April 1, 2026; everyone by April 1, 2028. No penalties before Sept. 1, 2026.
rule.textEn: Under the Hanson-Milone Act, anyone born after Jan. 1, 1989 needs a boater safety certificate to run a motorboat or PWC since April 1, 2026; older operators must have one by April 1, 2028.
rule.textEs: Según la Ley Hanson-Milone, quien nació después del 1 de enero de 1989 necesita un certificado de seguridad náutica para manejar una lancha o moto acuática desde el 1 de abril de 2026; los demás deberán tenerlo a más tardar el 1 de abril de 2028.

minAge.note: PWC only from 16, even with a certificate. The course is open from 12. Someone over 12 without a certificate may operate under direct supervision of a certified person over 18.

exemptions: Direct supervision by a certified person over 18 (operator over 12).
Holders of a valid merchant mariner credential or similar license.
Non-residents with a certificate from another U.S. state or territory or Canada.
Active military, National Guard or Coast Guard members qualified to run motorboats.
New owners within 6 months of buying a numbered or documented boat, with a temporary certificate.
Commercial fishing vessel operators; students in an approved course; approved boating safety programs.
Paddlecraft without a motor; USCG-documented vessels are not motorboats under the Act.

card.feeNote: The state charges no fee for the course or certificate; MEP classes are free, private providers may charge. Replacement via ilostmycard.com.

nonResident: Visitors with a certificate from any U.S. state or territory or from Transport Canada are exempt; Massachusetts residents need a Massachusetts certificate (out-of-state ones can be converted).
rental: Renters are not exempt; the Environmental Police is studying temporary certificates for low-power rentals.
pwcExtra: PWC operators must be 16 or older and hold a certificate.
penalty: $50 first offense, $100 for later offenses; no penalties before Sept. 1, 2026.

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau
sources.quote: People born after January 1, 1989, must have a boater safety certificate to operate a motorboat after April 1, 2026.

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau
sources.quote: People born on or before January 1, 1989, must have a boater safety certificate to operate a motorboat by April 1, 2028.

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau
sources.quote: MEP will not issue any penalties related to boater safety certificates before September 1, 2026.

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau
sources.quote: A motorboat is any vessel propelled by machinery, even if it is not the main or only source of propulsion.

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau
sources.quote: PWC operators must be at least 16 years of age and must have a boater safety certificate.

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau
sources.quote: A person over 12 years old who does not have a boater safety certificate can operate a motorboat if they are directly supervised by a person with a certificate who is over 18 years of age.

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau
sources.quote: Non-residents with a boater safety certificate or similar document from another U.S. state or territory or Canada.

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau
sources.quote: Massachusetts residents cannot use an out-of-state certificate when operating on the waters of the commonwealth.

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau
sources.quote: Operators with a valid, unexpired merchant mariner credential or similar license.

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau
sources.quote: Massachusetts does not currently charge a fee to take a boating safety education course. However, course providers may charge a fee.

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau
sources.quote: MEP-approved boating safety education courses can be taken either online or in person.

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau
sources.quote: The certificate is valid for life unless it is revoked.

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau
sources.quote: Violations may result in a fine of $50 for a first offense or $100 for a second or subsequent offense.

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau
sources.quote: MEP is considering options for temporary certificates for lower-power motorboat rentals.

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau
sources.quote: Students must be at least 12 years of age at the time of the course.
